- For customers that select a specific region (e.g., us-west-2, europe-west1, etc.), will inference payloads, embeddings, and logs be stored exclusively in that region for AWS / GCP / Azure?

Thanks Sally — looping in Laura (Infra Compliance) and Vivek (Product) to confirm specifics. Quick summary from my side:

- Residency: Redwood can pin inference request/response payloads and embeddings to a customer-selected region within the same cloud provider (AWS/GCP/Azure) for hosted marketplace listings.
- Retention defaults: request/response payloads & audit logs: 90 days; KV cache: ephemeral and per-instance (not a durable store); backups/snapshots: retained 30 days by default, can be configured with the Dedicated/Private offering.
- Deletion: we support account-level deletion requests; deletion triggers purging from active stores and cache. There is an audit log entry for deletion requests. Typical purge completion: within 24–72 hours for hosted; Private deployments follow customer policy.

Laura/Vivek — can you confirm the above and call out any provider-specific caveats (e.g., snapshot replication behavior on Azure or long-lived logs for GCP monitoring)? I attached a short Residency overview and a working matrix (residency_matrix_v1.xlsx) to help.

If helpful, I'm happy to join a 30-minute call with Marketplace Ops later this week.

Thanks,

On Tue, Jun 30, 2026 at 11:03 AM karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> Karthik: can you confirm the above and call out any provider-specific caveats?

Hi all — quick technical clarifications / bulleted answers below. TL;DR: hosted marketplace listings can be region-pinned per cloud provider; deletions are supported and we can provide an evidence artifact, with the caveats noted.

Provider specifics (summary):
- AWS (recommended pattern): inference payloads and embeddings stored in the selected AWS region (e.g., us-west-2). Backups are region-local snapshots by default; we do offer an option for cross-region replication for resilience but that is a paid opt-in and will be disclosed in the listing metadata. CloudTrail-style audit logs are retained in-region for 90 days.
- GCP: payloads and embeddings reside in the chosen GCP region. Stackdriver/Operations logs historically are global by default; we can configure region-scoped log sinks on a per-account basis to keep logs within the region — requires a configuration flag during onboarding.
- Azure: data-at-rest stays in customer-selected region. Azure incremental snapshots are stored in the same region; however, platform-managed monitoring artifacts (diagnostic settings) sometimes route to a workspace that could be in a paired region — we can request regional placement but need to document this in the Marketplace listing.

Retention & deletion specifics: 
- Request/response payloads: default 90 days retained in-region; can be shortened to meet customer requirements for enterprise deals.
- KV cache: in-memory/ephemeral at runtime; does not persist across instance termination. Not considered long-term storage.
- Audit logs: 90 days default; exportable to customer-owned sinks for longer retention.
- Backups/snapshots: default 30 days; cross-region replication is opt-in.
- Deletion flow: customer requests deletion via API/Support; system marks the account for purge, triggers async deletion across object stores, index services, and KV caches, and emits an audit event. For hosted marketplace customers, purge completion is typically 24–72 hours depending on data volume and whether cross-region replication was enabled. Private deployments: follow customer's retention config and deletion SLA.

Evidence for Marketplace Ops: we can produce a deletion report (timestamped audit event + list of purged object ids) and a signed attestation that purge steps completed. For SOC2/Security artifacts, I can attach our SOC2 summary and internal runbook on deletion procedures if Ops needs them.

Next steps: I'll update the residency_matrix_v1.xlsx with provider columns and the retention/deletion cells for the marketplace. If Marketplace Ops needs an explicit SLA clause, Karthik — I can propose a short paragraph.

Laura Bennett
Director, Infrastructure Compliance
Redwood Inference

Sally — thanks. Attached is a short draft clause and a sample attestation we typically provide to marketplace partners. We can commit to the following for hosted marketplace customers who opt into region-pinning: 

- Residency commitment: inference payloads and embeddings will be stored in the customer-selected region within the same cloud provider (AWS/GCP/Azure) for the duration of the customer's active subscription.
- Deletion SLA: Redwood will complete account-level purge of customer inference payloads, embeddings, and related in-platform artifacts within 72 hours of a validated deletion request (shorter SLAs can be negotiated for larger enterprise deals).
- Evidence: Redwood will provide a time-stamped deletion report (audit event + list of purged object identifiers) and a signed attestation on completion.

Suggested contract language (please feel free to redline):
"Redwood will persist customer inference data and embeddings in the cloud region specified by the customer for hosted marketplace listings. Upon receipt of a validated deletion request, Redwood will initiate and complete a purge of the customer’s inference payloads, embeddings, and associated in-platform artifacts within seventy-two (72) hours and provide a deletion report and signed attestation confirming completion"

I've also added the updated residency matrix to the shared Confluence page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Residency+Marketplaces+Checklist

If that works, can we set a short call next week to finalize the wording and confirm Marketplace's acceptance?

Thanks,
